articles.title: Supreme Court Agrees to Hear Challenge to Trump's Border Asylum Ban
articles.excerpt: The justices will decide whether President Trump's January 2025 proclamation lawfully shut off asylum at the southern border — a policy two lower courts rejected but that remains in force, with a ruling expected by summer 2027.
articles.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C., photographed at dusk. The court agreed on November 13 to decide whether the president's border asylum ban is lawful.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling will define how far a president's border-emergency powers reach over the asylum process — a pathway used by many Indian and other diaspora families' relatives fleeing persecution.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UK Study Visa Refusal Rate Hits 6.4%, Highest in Over a Decade
articles.excerpt: Home Office data for the year to September 2026 show refusals more than doubling in a year, withdrawals up nearly fivefold in the peak quarter, and credibility interviews failing four in five applicants called.
articles.image_caption: Chart: total long-term non-EU immigration to the UK by visa type, December 2019 to December 2025 — as UK study visa refusals hit 6.4%, the highest rate in over a decade.
articles.nri_angle: Indian students are one of the largest groups applying to UK universities, and a 6.4% refusal rate — with credibility interviews deciding most cases — changes how families should prepare an application.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UK Net Migration Falls to 77,000, Its Lowest Level Since 1997
articles.excerpt: Provisional ONS figures for the year to June 2026 show net migration more than halved in a year, driven by fewer non-EU arrivals for work and study — with Indians still the largest non-EU nationality coming to Britain.
articles.image_caption: A traveller walks through an airport departure terminal at sunset.
articles.nri_angle: Indians remain the largest non-EU nationality moving to the UK even as overall net migration hits a near-three-decade low, with study still the main route in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Second Judge Blocks Trump's New Birthright Citizenship Order
articles.excerpt: Judge Christopher Cooper's injunction bars three federal agencies from enforcing the August order against children in the class action, joining a Maryland block issued in September.
articles.image_caption: File photograph: protesters hold a 'Hands Off Birthright Citizenship' banner outside the US Supreme Court in Washington during earlier demonstrations over the policy.
articles.nri_angle: Children born in the US to parents in the order's new categories — including foreign-government and international-organization staff — remain citizens while both injunctions stand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Boston Man Wins $1 Million Lottery Prize, Then ICE Arrests Him
articles.excerpt: Ariel Velasquez-Morales claimed a $1 million Massachusetts Lottery prize on November 18. Six days later ICE arrested him in East Boston under a removal order issued in 2014.
articles.image_caption: Ariel Velasquez-Morales, the East Boston man who won a $1 million Massachusetts Lottery prize. ICE arrested him on November 24 under a removal order issued in 2014.
articles.nri_angle: A final removal order never expires: ICE executed a 2014 order against a man whose only new visibility was a lottery winner's photograph.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada Invites 6,000 French-Speaking Candidates at CRS Cut-Off of 401
articles.excerpt: The November 25 Express Entry draw was the 13th French-language round of 2026, taking the category to 66,500 invitations this year, with a profile cut-off of September 12.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian applicants in Canada's pool, the French-language category remains the lowest cut-off route to an invitation, at 401 against 519 for the last Canadian Experience Class draw.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Louisiana Visa Fraud Ringleader Patel Sentenced to 10 Years, Faces Removal
articles.excerpt: Chandrakant Patel recruited foreign nationals and paid four Louisiana law-enforcement leaders to certify fictitious armed robbery reports supporting fraudulent U visa applications, USCIS said.
articles.nri_angle: A fraud built on fake U visa claims warns diaspora applicants against paid intermediaries promising status through fabricated documents.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Judge Gives US Until Wednesday to Justify Holding Princeton Student Eva Yi Xie
articles.excerpt: The government must show by 5 p.m. Wednesday why Xie's detention differs from other recent ICE cases, or she gets a bond hearing. Princeton students rallied Monday and Rep. Watson Coleman called the detention outrageous.
articles.nri_angle: The case is a live test of whether a pending asylum claim protects a researcher from detention, watched closely by international students and scholars across US campuses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DHS Proposes Ending Deference on Visa Extensions, Affecting About 208,000 Petitions a Year
articles.excerpt: A one-sentence proposed rule would delete the regulation requiring USCIS to defer to its prior approvals on Form I-129 extensions — and DHS's own data says the main effect would be about 6,000 more evidence requests a year, not more denials.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-born workers received 77.6% of H-1B continuing-employment approvals in fiscal 2025, so a fresh-review standard for extensions would fall most heavily on Indian professionals and their families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Immigration Court Memo Cuts Key Filing Deadlines to 10 Days
articles.excerpt: EOIR's Policy Memorandum 27-02, effective November 23, replaces month-long and 60-day filing windows with 10-day deadlines for represented respondents in removal cases.
articles.image_caption: Map of Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) immigration court locations in the United States. A new court memo cuts key filing deadlines to 10 days.

sources.label: EOIR Policy Memorandum 27-02 (US Department of Justice)

articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals in US removal proceedings with counsel must now be ready to file pleadings, evidence and relief applications within 10 days of court orders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

rows: Written pleadings and evidence on removability

articles.title: CBI Brings Haryana Murder Accused Ashish Kumar Back From Kazakhstan
articles.excerpt: An INTERPOL Red Notice issued in September led officers to Ashish Kumar at Almaty immigration; Haryana Police took him into custody on arrival in New Delhi on November 23.
articles.nri_angle: The case shows the Red Notice and BHARATPOL route by which accused persons who flee India are located abroad and returned to face trial.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 12,700 Indian Tech Professionals Returned From the US in Nine Months, Xpheno Data Shows
articles.excerpt: Returns on the India–US corridor rose from 7,200 in 2023 to 15,100 in 2025, and 2026 is on pace to approach that record — but with about 14,500 moving the other way, the flow remains two-way, and the figures are recruitment-data estimates, not a government count.
articles.nri_angle: Indian tech workers in the US weighing a return can see the measured scale of the flow, what the Xpheno estimates do and do not count, and exactly who the $100,000 H-1B payment does and does not apply to.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: House Bill Would Let Deportation Orders Expire After 10 Years and Open a Green Card Path
articles.excerpt: The Protect Our Neighbors Act, introduced by four California Democrats, would put a 10-year expiry on final removal orders and let some longtime residents apply for permanent residence.

sources.label: Office of Rep. Lateefah Simon — Press Release
CiVL — House Democrats introduce a bill to let deportation orders expire after ten years

articles.nri_angle: About 1.19 million people live under final US removal orders, including long-settled Indian residents like Harjit Kaur; the bill would let orders expire after 10 years and open a discretionary green card path — but it is a proposal, not law.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Persistent Says Employee Immigration Data May Be Exfiltrated From US Law Firm
articles.excerpt: The breach was at a US law firm handling Persistent's immigration matters, not the company's own systems, the Pune IT major told stock exchanges — without naming the firm or how many employees are affected.
articles.image_caption: The Persistent Systems logo on a phone screen against a stock-market chart. The company told stock exchanges that employee immigration data may have been exfiltrated from a US law firm it engages, while its own systems remain secure.
articles.nri_angle: Persistent employees with US immigration cases are the affected group; the filing names no action or deadline, so the next step to watch is direct notification to affected individuals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Texas State Employee Faces Losing His Job as DACA Renewal Stalls
articles.excerpt: Juan Rodriguez filed to renew his DACA work permit in April. It is still pending, and the permit that supports his state job expires in December.
articles.nri_angle: Renewal delays that outrun USCIS's own 120-day goal are the practical risk for work-authorized immigrants, including Indian-origin DACA holders and their employers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Princeton PhD Student Eva Yi Xie Detained by ICE After Neuroscience Conference
articles.excerpt: Her lawyers say a pending asylum claim lets her stay; ICE says she never had authorisation to study in the US. A federal judge has barred her removal from Virginia while her habeas petition is heard.
articles.image_caption: A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement badge, in an Associated Press photograph. Princeton doctoral student Eva Yi Xie was detained by ICE at Reagan National Airport on November 19, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: The detention happened on a domestic flight by a researcher with a pending asylum claim — a concrete reminder for international students and scholars in the US to verify their status with a lawyer before travelling, even inside the country.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NRI Seafarers Can Now Use a Job Contract or Seaman's Book to Open an NPS Account
articles.excerpt: PFRDA's November 13 circular lets NRI seafarers use a valid employment contract or a Continuous Discharge Certificate with a disembarkation record under six months old as proof of address for NPS Tier I accounts.
articles.nri_angle: Removes the overseas-address-proof barrier that kept NRI seafarers — a large Indian maritime workforce — out of NPS pension accounts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ICE Holds Texas Store Worker After Jail Term Over Customer's Private Photos
articles.excerpt: Raghul Anandakrishnan, 29, was convicted of attempted invasive visual recording after a customer said he tried to AirDrop her intimate photos to himself. ICE took him from the Travis County jail and will hold him pending immigration court proceedings.
articles.nri_angle: Shows how a local criminal conviction can move a non-citizen directly into ICE detention, and why sharing a phone passcode at a retail counter carries real risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ICE Arrests Two on Sea-Tac Jetway, Delaying Los Angeles-Bound Flight
articles.excerpt: Washington's governor called the jetway arrests 'deeply un-American' and urged airlines to push ICE out of airports; Alaska Airlines said it had no advance notice.
articles.image_caption: A passenger is handcuffed by officers during an arrest at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on Saturday. ICE said the operation targeted a man who had overstayed his visa, and a second passenger was also arrested.
articles.nri_angle: Airport arrests of visa overstayers are directly relevant to diaspora travelers with pending applications or past overstays flying US domestic routes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Deported in 1999, Brooklyn Man Can Still Seek Sale of Home Bought in 1985, Court Rules
articles.excerpt: New York's Appellate Division held that because Clyde Nelson's 2007 divorce never disposed of the Brooklyn house, his ownership share survived — and his former wife cannot use the divorce to block his partition claim.
articles.image_caption: The Brooklyn skyline in New York. A state appeals court ruled on November 18 that a co-owner removed from the US in 1999 can still seek the sale of a Brooklyn home bought in 1985.
articles.nri_angle: The ruling shows removal from the US does not erase deed rights, and that a divorce silent on property leaves a deported spouse's share intact.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
